title: When a Street Changes
sentences: The street I grew up on has become almost unrecognisable over the course of twenty years.
The garage became a cafe, and the cafe was later converted into three small flats.
Property prices rose steadily and without interruption for roughly fifteen years.
The families who had lived there longest were the first to leave.
It would be easy to describe all of this as decline, and it would be inaccurate.
The street is safer, cleaner and considerably better served than it has ever been.
What has disappeared is harder to name than what has arrived.
There is nobody living there now who remembers my grandmother or her small garden.
A neighbourhood is partly buildings and partly a shared memory.
Only one of those two things can be rebuilt once enough money becomes available.
